approachQuestion.prompt:
Square panel budget

You have N unit tiles. Return the largest nonnegative integer side s such that an s-by-s square uses at most N tiles. Tiles may remain unused.

Example 1: N=35 -> 5.
Example 2: N=36 -> 6.
Example 3: N=0 -> 0.

Constraints and assumptions: 0 <= N <= 10^18. All intermediates must fit signed 64-bit integers. Return an exact integer result. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Binary-search the largest feasible s in [0,N], using upper midpoint low+floor((high-low+1)/2). Test positive mid with mid<=N/mid instead of multiplying; handle N=0 directly.
options.feedback: The feasibility predicate is monotone. Division avoids overflowing a large squared midpoint and upper-mid updates guarantee progress.

options.text: Start s=0 and increment while the next positive side is at most N divided by that side. Return the last feasible side.
options.feedback: The guarded test is exact, but advancing one side at a time makes avoidable progress compared with interval halving.

options.text: Binary-search [0,N] but test each midpoint by multiplying mid*mid in signed 64-bit arithmetic.
options.feedback: For N=10^18, the first midpoint is about 5*10^17; squaring it cannot be represented.

options.text: Round a floating-point square root to the nearest integer and return it without an integer check.
options.feedback: For N=35 the nearest integer to its root is 6, which needs 36 tiles; floor rather than nearest is required.

feedback.reason: Search an integer root using a safe monotone comparison instead of floating rounding.
details: If N=0 return 0. Use an upper-mid binary search over [0,N]. At positive mid, test mid<=floor(N/mid); on success set low=mid, otherwise set high=mid-1. Return low.

The predicate mid<=N/mid tests whether mid² fits without forming a potentially unsafe square. Upper midpoint and low=mid ensure progress when two candidates remain. Handle N=0 before dividing by a candidate.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (safe-root-search). Let N be the tile count. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(1 + log(N + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(1 + log(N + 1)) time, O(1 + log(N + 1)) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Binary search halves the integer-root interval using scalar bounds.
details: Binary search halves an interval initially of length N+1 until one integer remains. All arithmetic is bounded, with a constant number of endpoints and temporaries. No recursive calls or input copies are made.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(1 + log(N + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct for iterative interval halving, including N=0.
“O(sqrt(N) + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes incrementing the side one by one.
“O(1 + log(N + 1)) time, O(1 + log(N + 1)) auxiliary space”: The binary search is iterative rather than recursive.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: There is no unit-cost exact-root primitive in the analyzed method.
